definitions.explanation: A piece of lumber sawn into a square or rectangular cross-section, used as a structural member in carpentry and DIY work. The opposite of round timber ({丸太|まるた}).

examples.japanese: {角材|かくざい}を{二本|にほん}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought two pieces of square lumber.

examples.japanese: {角材|かくざい}を{切|き}って{棚|たな}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I cut some square lumber and built a shelf.

examples.japanese: {床|ゆか}を{支|ささ}える{角材|かくざい}が{老朽化|ろうきゅうか}していたので{交換|こうかん}した。
examples.english: The square timbers supporting the floor had deteriorated, so I replaced them.

notes:
Sold by cross-section size (e.g., {2|に}×{4|よん}{材|ざい} for two-by-four). Standard stock at hardware stores and lumber yards.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {角材|かくざい}を{切|き}る: to cut square lumber
- {木製|もくせい}の{角材|かくざい}: wooden square timber
- {太|ふと}い{角材|かくざい}: thick square timber

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {丸太|まるた}: round timber; log — uncut, round cross-section
- {板材|いたざい}: plank lumber — flat boards
- {木材|もくざい}: lumber; timber — general term covering all forms
